title: performance-canary-adaptive-sensitivity-rollout-guards
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: The existing perf canary detects regressions using fixed thresholds which leads to noisy rollouts for workloads with varying KV cache hit rates and sequence-length distributions. This PR introduces an adaptive sensitivity model and hysteresis-based rollout guards so the canary only blocks rollouts on sustained, meaningful regressions and adapts thresholds based on observed workload characteristics.

Summary of changes: Implement an adaptive sensitivity detector that adjusts latency and throughput thresholds at canary time by factoring in KV-cache hit percentage, median sequence length, and observed batching behavior; add hysteresis windows to require sustained deviation before triggering a rollback; introduce per-model and per-route guard configurations with safe defaults; surface additional diagnostic metrics to the Console and canary reports.

Design highlights: 1) Detector computes baseline with weighted percentiles (50/90/99) over a sliding window (default 30m). 2) Sensitivity scale derived from KV-hit rate and median seq len: low KV-hit -> higher tolerance for tail latency; long med seq -> scale expected token latency. 3) Hysteresis: two-stage trigger (warning + violation) with configurable window and required consecutive windows before rollback. 4) Auto-backoff: when violation is detected, traffic shift is capped and a staged rollback is scheduled unless human override. 5) Compatibility: integrates with existing perf-canary pipeline and rollout-engine; configuration stored under canary policy object and exposed via API.

Testing and verification: unit tests for threshold math, integration tests in perf-canary harness, end-to-end synthetic workloads in perf-lab (GPU and CPU profiles), KV-hits simulated to validate scale behavior, warm canaries run on staging with production-like traffic.

Migration notes: existing canary policies keep current fixed-threshold mode by default; customers can opt-in to adaptive mode via policy flag: "adaptive_sensitivity: true". We ship with conservative defaults to avoid false positives.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector algorithm implementation (runtime + config)
- [x] Hysteresis and staged rollback logic
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Perf-lab validation runs
- [x] Console metrics and canary report UI hooks
- [x] Documentation and Linear links

Links: Linear ENG-4132, ENG-4210. Related PRs: refs to previous perf-canary hysteresis work.

Notes: This description is intentionally compact; see inline doc comments and the canary policy schema for configuration details.

release_notes: Enhancement: canary rollout guards now support adaptive sensitivity based on KV cache hit rate and sequence-length distribution. Adds hysteresis to reduce noisy rollbacks and staged rollback policy for safer rollouts. Configurable per-policy; conservative defaults preserve existing behavior.
sensitivity_tuning: adaptive hysteresis with KV-aware thresholds and clamped multiplier range
notes_for_ops: Monitor canary.report.canary_latency_scaled and canary.report.kv_hit_rate for first 72h after deploy; watch for any unexpected increase in manual rollbacks. Ops can opt-out by setting policy.adaptive_sensitivity=false.
qa_summary: Validated on perf-lab with 10 runs each for high/low KV hit scenarios; staging canaries ran with production traffic slice (1%) for 48h with no false positives; synthetic regression injected to validate rollback path.
